conventions.convention: Countable Choice means that every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function; the physical conclusions retain this mathematical assumption.
V is real H1-zero with gradient norm; Q is real L2 with spatial mean zero and its L2 norm. Pressure outputs use this selected gauge.
The creeping branch adopts zero inertia as an alternative model, with stress −pI + 2μD and force balance div σ + ρb = 0; it does not simultaneously impose material-acceleration momentum balance.

Density and dynamic viscosity are primitive positive branch parameters in SI units. Kinematic viscosity μ/ρ is derived. Stress divergence is rowwise, and stationary no-slip data are separately adopted.

The scaling is x = ℓ0 y, physical time = (ℓ0/U0)t*, physical velocity = U0 u*, physical pressure = ρ0 U0² p*, and ν* = μ0/(ρ0 U0 ℓ0). Physical volume-time pressure observations consequently acquire the factor ρ0 U0 ℓ0⁴.

The evolutionary result explicitly adopts a distributional physical balance at the stated Sobolev regularity. It uses mass-projected initialization, interval-average forcing, any actual mixed backward-Euler MINI root, and τmax Λ ≤ 1/2. Pressure estimates concern primitives and smooth time tests, not instantaneous pressure error.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, the stated forced incompressible Newtonian weak extension, complete smooth MINI interface hypotheses, and τmax Λ ≤ 1/2, the endpoint velocity observation error is at most (ν*)^(−1/2) C* H times the weighted sensor norm. The nodal pressure-primitive observation error is at most K H times the Q norm of ξ, and the smooth time-tested pressure error is at most (K+1) H times the L1 norm of η′ and the Q norm of ξ. Physical volume-time pressure bounds acquire the factor ρ0 U0 ℓ0⁴. These are conditional strong-branch predictions, with no instantaneous pressure-error or Reynolds-uniform claim.

The parameterized forced creeping Stokes weak formulation uses V = H1-zero(D*; R³), Q = L2-zero-mean(D*), ν* = μ0/(ρ0 U0 ℓ0), Fg*(v) = ∫ g*·v, and the equations 2ν*∫ ε(u*):ε(v) − ∫ q* div v = Fg*(v), −∫ r div u* = 0. Physical pressure is ρ0 U0² q*, and the stationary no-slip condition is encoded by V. This weak interface contains no material-acceleration term.

For the specified classical fields, positive constant density and viscosity, and prescribed continuous body acceleration, the forced branch adopts div u = 0 and ρ0(∂t u + (u·∇)u) = ρ0 b + div σ, with σ = −pI3 + 2μ0D and D = (∇u + ∇uᵀ)/2. Stationary no-slip boundary data are separately selected.

Under Countable Choice and the stated bounded connected Lipschitz-domain, positive-parameter, continuous L2 body-acceleration, forced creeping-model and bounded real-linear pressure-sensor hypotheses, the physical pressure-output difference is at most 3ρ0 U0² Cdiv(D*) CP(D*) (Σj ||Sj||²)^(1/2) ||g1*−g2*||L2. This is conditional stability for the adopted creeping model, without a finite-Reynolds Navier–Stokes approximation claim.

concerns.concern: The Statement first defines t_m as a dimensionless partition node, but later says “For t_m=(ℓ0/U0)t_m*”. The symbol t_m* has not been defined, and t_m is thereby reused as physical time. The intended conversion is clear from the surrounding scaling, but distinct names for the dimensionless and physical nodes are needed.

seams_checked.note: The consumer treats stationary no-slip as separately adopted boundary data. Its weak interfaces explicitly encode zero trace rather than claiming that the boundary postulate supplies general Lipschitz-domain solvability.

The consumers preserve the Newtonian stress sign, constant-density incompressibility, pressure-multiplier interpretation and derived kinematic viscosity. The forced definition explicitly adds prescribed body acceleration to the unforced model.

The creeping theorem uses the same real spaces, mean-zero gauge, bounded sensors, continuous load and 3 Cdiv pressure-stability constant. Poincare supplies the additional load factor CP; physical pressure scaling supplies ρ0 U0².

The no-slip theorem retains the full smooth MINI interface, initialization, forcing averages, actual-root condition, time-step restriction and explicit constants. It correctly restricts pressure conclusions to primitives and smooth time tests. Its Sobolev physical balance is explicitly adopted.

The forced creeping branch preserves the postulate's prescribed body acceleration and alternative zero-inertia force law. It does not infer that branch from small Reynolds number or claim a Navier–Stokes approximation error.
